BiblicalUsage: gôbahh is the word for height, exaltation, haughtiness. In 1 Samuel 17:4, the text says "whose height [was] six cubits and a span." In 2 Chronicles 3:4, the text says "and the height [was] an hundred and twenty."
TheologicalSignificance: I take gôbahh to mean that pride is the oldest sin, and it always ends the same way — brought low. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: David and Goliath; Building of Solomon's Temple
